You can use various tenses in your writing to relate events or tell stories.

You can write in narrative tenses when you want to tell a story or recall past events. The tenses are the Simple Past, Past Continuous and Past Perfect. You can use these tenses in the affirmative, negative and interrogative form (questions).
Remember not to mix present and past tenses when you are narrating.
Sojourner Truth, a self-given name, was born a slave in 1797.
She and her family were living on an estate, north of New York, until 1806.
In 1700, the state of New York was beginning to start the negotiations that would lead to the abolition of slavery.
During the Civil War, Truth helped the Union recruit black men to be troops.
Soon after, she petitioned the court to secure the release of one of her children who had been taken to the South.

Sojourner Truth, a self-given name, was born a slave in 1797. Her father,
James Baumfree, was captured and put into slavery and her mother Mau-Mau Bet,
came from a family of slaves transported from Guinea. She and her family were living on an
estate, north of New York, until 1806. At 9 years old, Truth was sold at an auction along with a flock of sheep for $100. She was sold off to a number of demanding, abusive slave owners, finally coming to live and work in West Park, New York.

It was during this period that Truth, who had only spoken Dutch before this, learned English. In 1700, the state of New York was beginning to start the negotiations that would lead to the abolition of slavery. They emancipated all slaves in 1827. Soon after, she petitioned the court to secure the release of one of her children who had been taken to the South. Her case, where a black woman was successful in challenging a white man in a US court, was groundbreaking. In 1843, Truth dropped her slave name, Isabella Baumfree. From then on, she devoted her life to the Methodist Church and to abolishing slavery. Furthermore, she joined the Northampton Association of Education and Industry, a group dedicated to the fight for rights for women and pacifism.

During the Civil War, Truth helped the Union recruit black men to be troops. On
several occasions, she met with President Abraham Lincoln to discuss her beliefs
and experiences. Sojourner Truth died on November 26th, 1883, and is buried
beside other members of her family at Battle Creek. This determined and courageous woman
spoke passionately on women's rights, prison reform, and universal
suffrage for the latter part of her life.
